is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae sensu lato, specifically An. arabiensis and An. gambiae s.s. (Page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports Ace-1 G280S (referred to as G119S) mutation frequencies (Page 6, Table 2).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 provides genotype counts (GG, GS, SS) and sample sizes for both An. arabiensis and An. gambiae s.s. across four study sites (Page 6).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field breeding habitats in Kakamega County, Kenya (Page 2, Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original field collection and laboratory analysis data (Page 2-3, Methods).

sub_country_location.evidence: The study provides specific sub-county locations: Ikolomani, Mumias East, Lurambi, and Malava (Page 2, Methods).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The collection period is stated as October 2018 to March 2019 (Page 2, Methods).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a new, independent cross-sectional survey conducted in Kakamega County.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including genotype counts and bioassay results, are provided in the main text tables (Table 1, Table 2, Table 3).

assessment.summary: This study evaluated pirimiphos-methyl susceptibility and Ace-1 G119S mutation frequencies in Anopheles gambiae s.l. (An. arabiensis and An. gambiae s.s.) from four sub-counties in Kakamega, Kenya. It reports phenotypic resistance and genotype counts for the G119S mutation.
